questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code reports the outcome of replicated writes? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A follower receives Timeline(author, 20, true). What happens?
choices: It serves the read from its own FSM, since the data is replicated
It returns a NotLeaderError carrying the address of the node it believes is leader
It forwards the request to the leader and returns the result
It runs Barrier and then reads local state

questions.prompt: Why does the strong read path call Barrier after VerifyLeader succeeds?
choices: To make sure all entries committed before the read have been applied to the local FSM, so the read reflects them
To persist a snapshot of the FSM before reading
To demote other nodes so they stop serving reads
To extend the leader's lease so VerifyLeader does not have to be called again

questions.prompt: A leader accepts Apply, replicates the entry to a majority, then loses leadership before replying. What may the caller of Publish observe?
choices: Always a successful return, since the entry reached a majority
Always an error, and the entry is guaranteed not to have been applied
Possibly an error even though the entry was committed and will be applied on every replica
A panic from the FSM because the leader term changed
